question: Does the deployed price/variance kernel give calibrated 21-session 95% VaR and better CRPS than flat EWMA in a period never used to build or audit it?

data.source: data/history/prices (Yahoo chart API, split-adjusted closes plus dividend events)
data.adjustment: total-return factor from dividends: prior closes times (1 - dividend/previous close)

excluded.current_exposure basket: contains SGOV and was selected ex post

A_calibration.test: Kupiec unconditional coverage of 95% VaR, Holm over the four targets at 0.05
A_calibration.supported: no rejection and every exact 95% upper bound of the exception rate <= 0.12

B_improvement.interval: 3-origin block bootstrap, two-sided, alpha 0.05/3 per basket, seed 20261028
B_improvement.supported: at least one interval above zero and none below zero

limits: Answers only the risk component. It does not test return forecasts, fundamentals, the optimizer or net economic value. Adjusted current revisions, not original vintages; ETF list fixed today (survivorship mostly irrelevant for these funds, not for NVDA). No rejection is not a certificate. Results do not change production.
